selected_benchmarks.name: Split CIFAR-100
selected_benchmarks.note: Split into 10 or 20 tasks (10 or 5 classes each)

selected_baselines.name: EWC
selected_baselines.paper: Kirkpatrick et al., Overcoming catastrophic forgetting, PNAS 2017

selected_baselines.name: Experience Replay
selected_baselines.source: Custom: Maintain memory buffer of past examples
selected_baselines.paper: Chaudhry et al., Continual Learning with Tiny Episodic Memories, 2019

rationale: Split CIFAR-100 is the strongest available domain-standard benchmark for class-incremental image classification and supports average accuracy, forgetting, and backward transfer. CIFAR-10-C is useful only as a secondary distribution-shift stress test for task-agnostic routing; Split MNIST and Permuted MNIST are too simple for meaningful pretrained-ViT expert-memory conclusions, while Office-31 primarily targets domain adaptation. EWC supplies the classic regularization baseline, Experience Replay is a strong classic rehearsal baseline, PackNet represents parameter isolation, and LoRA is the most relevant modern parameter-efficient adaptation baseline in the supplied list. QLoRA is omitted because its principal contribution is quantized language-model adaptation rather than continual ViT routing.
experiment_notes: Use one frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT and identical normalized classifiers, data orders, augmentations, and calibration for every condition. Resize CIFAR inputs according to the pretrained ViT specification. Evaluate 10-task and, if feasible, 20-task Split CIFAR-100 without task IDs. Match trainable/stored parameters and active FLOPs; separately report measured latency, throughput, and peak VRAM. Apply CIFAR-10-C only at evaluation time to measure routing robustness under corruption, not as evidence of class-incremental learning by itself. The 300-second budget is insufficient for a publishable multi-seed ViT study, so use it only for a smoke test or cached-feature pilot; final claims require at least five paired seeds, preferably ten, with average accuracy, final accuracy, forgetting, backward transfer, and routing diagnostics.
